children.translated_text: Obeisance to Śrī <s>Gaṇeśa</s>.
Now begins the <s>Aparokṣānubhava</s> (Direct Experience [of Brahman]) with commentary.
Oṃ. I bow to Śrī <s>Hari</s>, the Supreme Bliss, the Teacher, the Lord,
the Pervader of all worlds, the Cause [of all]. ||1||
The <s>Aparokṣānubhūti</s> (Direct Experience) is indeed proclaimed for the attainment of liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>);
it should be examined again and again with effort by the virtuous. ||2||
Through the <s>dharma</s> of one's own <s>varṇa</s> (class) and <s>āśrama</s> (stage of life), through austerity (<s>tapas</s>), and through the satisfaction of <s>Hari</s>,
the fourfold means (<s>sādhana</s>) beginning with dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) becomes effective for a person. ||3||
Dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>) toward sense-objects — from [those of] <s>Brahmā</s> down to the immovable [plants] —
just as [one has] dispassion toward crow's excrement — that indeed is pure [dispassion]. ||4||

children.text: दो० । शंकर स्वामी जो कत्यो अप्रोक्ष अनुभव जोह ।। सोभाषा
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] <s>Dohā</s>: What <s>Śaṅkara Svāmī</s> composed — the <s>Aparokṣa Anubhava</s> — that I now

children.text: करि कहतहौं जेहि समझै सबंकोइ १ ग्रंथ चौपाई । श्रीहरि
children.translated_text: render in the vernacular so that everyone may understand. ||1|| [Hindi:] <s>Caupāī</s>: Śrī <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: परमानंद रूपजो । उपदेष्टा अरु ईश्वर है सो ।। ब्यापक सब
children.translated_text: who is of the form of Supreme Bliss, who is the Teacher and the Lord —

children.text: लोकन को कारन ।। ताहिनमो मैं करौं हजारन ।। मोक्ष सिद्ध
children.translated_text: the Pervader, the Cause of all worlds — to Him I bow thousands of times.

children.text: को अर्थ सुजीई । ज्ञान प्रत्यक्ष कहौं मैं सोई ।। ताते साधजनो
children.translated_text: For the purpose of the attainment of liberation, O good ones, I shall speak of

children.text: यत्नन करि । पुनि पुनि यह बिचार हिय में धरि २ अपनोबर-
children.translated_text: that direct knowledge. Therefore, O virtuous ones, with effort, consider this again and again, holding it in the heart. ||2||

children.text: णाश्रम धर्म जोई। तेहि तपकरि प्रसन्न हरि होई ।। साधन होत
children.translated_text: Whatever is the <s>dharma</s> of one's own <s>varṇa</s> and <s>āśrama</s> — through that austerity, <s>Hari</s> becomes pleased.

children.text: पुरुष को चारि । बैराग्यादि सुलेहु निहारि ३ चार साधन कहिये
children.translated_text: The fourfold means arise for a person: dispassion and the rest — understand them well. ||3|| The four means are said to be: dispassion (<s>vairāgya</s>), discrimination (<s>viveka</s>), tranquility (<s>śama</s>), self-control (<s>dama</s>), etc., and the desire for liberation (<s>mumukṣutva</s>). First, the nature of dispassion is described.

children.text: हैं बैराग्य बिबेक शम दमादि मुमुक्षु प्रथम बैराग्य को स्वरूप
कहिये ।। चौ० ।। ब्रह्मादिक भुवि भोगहि जेते । काक बिष्ठ सम
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] <s>Caupāī</s>: All the enjoyments in the world from <s>Brahmā</s> downwards — know them as equal to crow's excrement.

children.text: जाने तेते ।। सोनिर्मल बैराग्यकहावै । रागादिक मलदूरिबहावै ४।।
children.translated_text: That is called pure dispassion; it washes away the impurity of attachment and the like. ||4||
Obeisance to Śrī <s>Gaṇeśa</s>. Now begins the vernacular rendering of the <s>Aparokṣānubhava</s> text.
The Self (<s>Ātman</s>) alone is of eternal nature; the visible [world] is its opposite [i.e., transient].
Such firm ascertainment is truly discrimination (<s>viveka</s>) of reality. ||5||
The constant abandonment of desires (<s>vāsanā</s>) is called tranquility (<s>śama</s>);
the restraint of the external [senses] is called self-control (<s>dama</s>). ||6||
The turning away from sense-objects — that is the supreme cessation (<s>uparati</s>);
the endurance of all sufferings is forbearance (<s>titikṣā</s>) — that is deemed auspicious. ||7||
Devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) to the words of scripture (<s>nigama</s>) and the teacher (<s>ācārya</s>) is well-known as faith (<s>śraddhā</s>);
the one-pointedness of mind on the true object is remembered as concentration (<s>samādhāna</s>). ||8||
'How shall I ever become free from the bondage of <s>saṃsāra</s>?' —
that firm resolve of the intellect is to be declared as the desire for liberation (<s>mumukṣutā</s>). ||9||

children.text: अब बिबेक को स्वरूप कहिये हैं ।। चौ० ।। नित्य आत्मा
रूपहि जानौ । दृश्य सकल बिनाशवत मानौ ।। ऐसो निश्चय
children.translated_text: regard all that is visible as perishable. When such firm

children.text: होवै जबहीं । भयो बिवेक जानिये तबहीं ५ अब षट् संपत्ति शम
children.translated_text: ascertainment arises — then know that discrimination has come about. ||5|| Now the six accomplishments (<s>ṣaṭsampatti</s>) — tranquility, self-control, etc. — are described.

children.text: दमादि कहिये हैं ।। सदा बासना त्यागि है जोई ।। शम स्वरूप
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] Whoever always abandons desires — that is said to be the nature of tranquility (<s>śama</s>).

children.text: कहियत है सोई ।। वाह्येंद्री वृत्ति निग्रहकरै । दमस्वरूप यह
children.translated_text: Whoever restrains the activity of the external senses — sages declare that to be the nature of self-control (<s>dama</s>).

children.text: मुनि उच्चरै ।। उपरति कहिये हैं ६ बिषयनते मन हटिरहै जोई ।
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] Cessation (<s>uparati</s>) is now described. ||6|| Whoever withdraws the mind from sense-objects —

children.text: परम उपरति कहावै सोई ।। सहनो सब दुःखन को जोई । सो
children.translated_text: that is called supreme cessation. The endurance of all suffering —

children.text: सुख रूप तितिक्षा होई ७ श्रुति गरुबाक्य बिषय बिश्वासा ।
children.translated_text: that is forbearance (<s>titikṣā</s>), which is of the nature of happiness. ||7|| Trust in the words of scripture and the teacher —

children.text: ताहि कहिय श्रद्धा सुप्रकासा ।। चितको रोक राखिबो जोई ।
children.translated_text: that is called faith (<s>śraddhā</s>), well-illuminated. And the restraining and holding of the mind —

children.text: समाधान कहियत है सोई ८ हे हरि यह जग बंधन जोई ।
children.translated_text: that is called concentration (<s>samādhāna</s>). ||8|| 'O <s>Hari</s>, this worldly bondage —

children.text: कैसे कब छूटैगो सोई ।। यह दृढ़ बुद्धि भई हे जाकों । सो मुमु-
children.translated_text: how and when shall I be freed from it?' — whoever has this firm resolve in the intellect,
that is called the desire for liberation (<s>mumukṣutā</s>). ||9||
[Hindi:] Now the nature of discrimination is described. <s>Caupāī</s>: Know the Self (<s>Ātman</s>) as eternal in form;
A person endowed with the said means should indeed
undertake inquiry (<s>vicāra</s>) for the attainment of knowledge, desiring the good of the Self. ||10||
Knowledge does not arise without inquiry — not through any other means;
just as the appearance of objects is never [possible] without light. ||11||
'Who am I? How was this [world] born? Who indeed is the maker of this?
What is the material cause here?' — such is this inquiry. ||12||
'I am not the aggregate of elements, not the body; nor am I the aggregate of the senses;
I am something distinct from all these' — such is this inquiry into truth. ||13||
'Everything arises from ignorance; through knowledge, everything is dissolved;
the manifold <s>saṃkalpa</s> (volition) is the doer' — such is this inquiry. ||14||

children.text: साधनचारकहे समुक्ताय । तिनकर पुरुष युक्तजोआय । तिह
विचारकरनोहे याते । ज्ञान सिद्धिके अर्थतुजाते १० बिना प्बईक्षार
children.translated_text: inquiry should be undertaken, for the purpose of the attainment of knowledge. ||10|| Without inquiry,

children.text: ज्ञान नहिं होह । साधन औरकरौ किंन कोङ्के ।। ज्यो सूर्यादि प्र-
children.translated_text: knowledge does not arise; what else can any other means accomplish?

children.text: काश विनाते । यस्तु घटादि नाहि न देखियते ११ मैं हौं कोजग
children.translated_text: Just as without light such as the sun, pots and the like cannot be seen. ||11|| Who am I? How was this

children.text: उपज्यो कति । जग को कर्ता कौन सुताते ।। अरुया जगको का-
children.translated_text: world born? Who is the maker of the world? And what is the

children.text: रण कनि । काको नाम विचारे तनि १२ भौतिक देह नहीं हो
children.translated_text: cause of this world? — reflect upon these, whose name is 'inquiry.' ||12|| I am not this

children.text: जाते । होंहन्भिन्सग्लमूह नहिताते ।। इनको साक्षी मैं हौं जनि ।
children.translated_text: elemental body; nor am I the aggregate of senses. I am the witness of all these —

children.text: याको नामबिचारै तनि १३ यह सद्य जग अज्ञानतेभय । ज्ञान
children.translated_text: know this; its name is 'inquiry.' ||13|| This entire world [arises] from ignorance; when knowledge arose,

children.text: भयजुलीन द्वे गयठ ।। बहुबिधि कर्त्ता संकल्प जौन । याको
children.translated_text: both dissolved together. The manifold doer-volition (<s>saṃkalpa</s>) —
its name is 'inquiry.' ||14||
[Hindi:] Having stated the four means, the person who is endowed with them — for him,
That which is the material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) of both [individual self and world] — one, subtle, eternal, and imperishable —
just as clay [is the cause] of pots and the like — such is this inquiry. ||15||
'I alone am one, subtle, the knower, the witness, eternal and imperishable;
that I am — there is no doubt in this' — such is this inquiry. ||16||
Those who see the unity of these two [Self and body] — what ignorance can be greater than this?
The Self (<s>Ātman</s>) is partless and one; the body is covered by many [sheaths]. ||17||
The Self is the inner controller; the body is the outer, controlled [entity];
those who see the unity of these two — what ignorance can be greater than this? ||18||
The Self is made of knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>), wise; the body is made of flesh, impure;
those who see the unity of these two — what ignorance can be greater than this? ||19||

children.text: याजग कारण एक सु जोई । सूक्षम सत अविनाशी सोई ।।
ज्यों घटादि कारण मृद जौने । याको नाम बिचारैतौन १५
children.translated_text: Just as clay is the cause of pots and the like — its name is 'inquiry.' ||15||

children.text: मैंहौं सूक्ष्म एकज्ञाता पुनि । साक्षी सत अविनाशी जो सुनि ।।
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] I am subtle, one, the knower; I am the witness, eternal, and imperishable — hear this.

children.text: सो मैं यामें संशय नाहीं । याको नाम बिचार सुआहीं १६ आत्मा
children.translated_text: That I am — there is no doubt in this. Its name is 'excellent inquiry.' ||16|| The Self

children.text: अकल एकहै जोई । देह बहुत करि आबृति सोई ।। तिन दोउ
children.translated_text: is partless and one; the body is wrapped in many [coverings].

children.text: एक सु देखै जौन ।। यातें परे अज्ञान सु कौन १७ आत्मा न्यामक
children.translated_text: Those who see these two as one — what ignorance can be greater than that? ||17|| The Self is the inner controller;

children.text: अंतर जोई । देह नियम्य वाह्य पुनि सोई ।। तिन दोउ एकसु
children.translated_text: the body is the outer, controlled [entity]. Those who see these two as one —

children.text: देखै जनि । याते परे अज्ञान सुकौन १८ आत्मा शुद्ध ज्ञानमय
children.translated_text: what ignorance can be greater than that? ||18|| The Self is pure, made of knowledge;

children.text: जोई । देह मांस मय अशुचि जुसोई ।। तिन दोउ एक सु देखै
children.translated_text: the body is made of flesh, impure. Those who see these two as one —
what ignorance can be greater than that? ||19||
[Hindi:] That which is the one cause of this world — it is subtle, eternal, and imperishable.
The Self is self-luminous, pure; the body is called <s>tāmasic</s> (dark, inert).
Those who see the unity of these two — what ignorance can be greater than this? ||20||
The Self is eternal, of the nature of existence (<s>sat</s>); the body is not eternal, of the nature of non-existence (<s>asat</s>).
Those who see the unity of these two — what ignorance can be greater than this? ||21||
The luminosity of the Self is such that it illuminates all objects;
the light of fire and the like is not like that, for at night [the world] becomes dark. ||22||
'I am this body' — the deluded person holds and persists [in this view], alas!
Even knowing 'this is mine' [i.e., the body belongs to me], like the sight of a pot [as separate from clay], always. ||23||
'I am <s>Brahman</s> alone, equal, peaceful, characterized by existence-consciousness-bliss (<s>saccidānanda</s>);
I am not this body of unreal nature' — this is called knowledge by the wise. ||24||

children.text: आत्मा स्वच्छ प्रकाशक जोई । देह तामसी जड़ है सोई ।
तिन दोउ एक सु देखै जौन । याते परे अज्ञान सुकौन २०
children.translated_text: Those who see these two as one — what ignorance can be greater than that? ||20||

children.text: आत्मा नित्यरु सत्य रूप जो । देह अनित्य असत्य मय हे सो ।।
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] The Self is eternal and of true nature; the body is impermanent and of unreal nature.

children.text: तिन दोउ एकसु देखै जौन । याते परे अज्ञान सुकौन २१ सो
children.translated_text: Those who see these two as one — what ignorance can be greater than that? ||21|| That

children.text: प्रकाश आत्माको तातें । सब पदार्थ भ्रासतहैं जातें ।। नहिं सूर्य्या-
children.translated_text: luminosity is of the Self, from which all objects are illuminated.

children.text: दि प्रकाश सु ऐसो । दिवस होत निशि होत न तैसो २२ मैं हौं
children.translated_text: The light of the sun and the like is not like this; day comes, but night is not [illuminated] thus. ||22|| 'I am

children.text: देह सुढ़ या इमि कहै । यह धरि रह्यो अज्ञ जन वहै ।। मम यह
children.translated_text: the body' — whoever says this firmly — that ignorant person persists in [this delusion].

children.text: देह जानि करि जोई । जिमि घट वृष्टि सर्बदा सोई २३ मैं हौं
children.translated_text: 'This body is mine' — knowing this, like [seeing] a pot always [as different from clay]. ||23|| I am

children.text: ब्रह्म शांत सम जोई । हौं सच्चिदानंद पुनि सोई ।। हों नहिं देह
children.translated_text: <s>Brahman</s>, peaceful, equal; I am existence-consciousness-bliss (<s>saccidānanda</s>).

children.text: असत जो आहि । बुधजन ज्ञान कहतहैं ताहि ।। २४ ।।
children.translated_text: I am not this body, which is unreal — the wise call that knowledge. ||24||
[Hindi:] The Self is pure and self-luminous; the body is <s>tāmasic</s> and inert.
I am changeless (<s>nirvikāra</s>), formless (<s>nirākāra</s>), faultless (<s>niravadya</s>), imperishable (<s>avyaya</s>);
I am not this body of unreal nature — this is called knowledge by the wise. ||25||
I am free from disease (<s>nirāmaya</s>), without appearance (<s>nirābhāsa</s>), without modification (<s>nirvikalpa</s>), all-pervading;
I am not this body of unreal nature — this is called knowledge by the wise. ||26||
I am without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), without action (<s>niṣkriya</s>), eternal (<s>nitya</s>), eternally free (<s>nityamukta</s>), stainless;
I am not this body of unreal nature — this is called knowledge by the wise. ||27||
I am pure (<s>nirmala</s>), immovable (<s>niścala</s>), infinite (<s>ananta</s>), pure, ageless (<s>ajara</s>), deathless (<s>amara</s>);
I am not this body of unreal nature — this is called knowledge by the wise. ||28||
Having abandoned the beautiful [name] 'person' (<s>puruṣa</s>) that is agreed upon for one's own body,
why, O fool, do you make the Self — which is beyond the body — into a void (<s>śūnya</s>)? ||29||

children.text: निर्विकार निराकारहों । अबिनाशी निरवद्य सारहों ।। होंनहिं
देह असत जो आहि । बुधजन ज्ञान कहत हैं ताहि २५ ।।
children.translated_text: I am not this body, which is unreal — the wise call that knowledge. ||25||

children.text: रोग रहित हों निराभास हों । निर्बिकल्प ब्यापक प्रकाश हों ।।
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] I am free from disease, without appearance; I am without modification, pervading, luminous.

children.text: होंनहिं देह असत्य जो आहि । बुधजन ज्ञान कहत हैं ताहि ।।
children.translated_text: I am not this body, which is unreal — the wise call that knowledge.

children.text: २६ ।। निर्गुण निष्क्रिय नित्य हों जोई । नित्यमुक्त अच्युत हों
children.translated_text: ||26|| I am without qualities, without action, eternal; I am

children.text: सोई ।। हों नहिं देह असत्य जो आहि । बुधजन ज्ञान अहत हैं
children.translated_text: eternally free, imperishable. I am not this body, which is unreal — the wise call that knowledge.

children.text: ताहि २७ हौं निर्मल निश्चल अनंत पुनि । शुद्धहों अजर
children.translated_text: ||27|| I am pure, immovable, and infinite; I am pure, ageless,

children.text: अमर निश्चय सुनि ।। होंनहिं देह असत्त जो आहि ।। बुधजन
children.translated_text: and deathless — know this with certainty. I am not this body, which is unreal. The wise

children.text: ज्ञान कहत हैं ताहि ।। हे मूरख आतम है जोई । देहातीत सुशो-
children.translated_text: call that knowledge. O fool, the Self — which is beyond the body and is most

children.text: भन सोई ।। श्रुतिकर बर्णित पुरुष पुरान । ताहि शून्य क्यों करत
children.translated_text: beautiful — it is described by scripture as the ancient <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: बखान २८ बचन का शिष्य बचन देह अतीत आपको पुरुष जा-
children.translated_text: Why do you call it void? ||28|| The meaning is: the disciple's saying that one should know oneself as the <s>Puruṣa</s> beyond the body — that is the name of knowledge.

children.text: नना इसका नाम ज्ञानहै सो शून्य हुआ गुरु बचन ब्रह्मी श्रुति
children.translated_text: That which became void [in wrong understanding] — the teacher's word, <s>Brahman</s>, scripture —
[all] declare the Self as distinct from the body. ||29||
[Hindi:] I am changeless, formless; I am imperishable and faultless in essence.
O fool, [know] the Self — through <s>śruti</s> (scripture), reasoning, and the person [himself] —
as beyond the body, of the nature of eternal existence, extremely difficult to see for those like you. ||30||
That which is renowned by the word 'I' — the supreme One alone abides;
having attained grossness and multiplicity, how can that person be identical with the body? ||31||
The 'I' is established as the seer; the body is situated as the seen;
from the indication 'this is mine' [i.e., 'this is my body'], how can that person be identical with the body? ||32||
The 'I' is free from modification, but the body is always subject to modification;
this is directly perceived — how can that person be identical with the body? ||33||
Since, having heard [the <s>śruti</s> declare the Self] as 'beyond all,' through that [<s>śruti</s>] the characteristics of the person
have been ascertained by the deluded one — how can that person be identical with the body? ||34||

children.text: चौ० । हे मूरुख सुन आतम जोहै ।। श्रुति युक्तिन करि
वर्णित सोहै ।। देहातीत हेतु जग जीई । अति अदृश्य
children.translated_text: have described it thus: beyond the body is the cause of the world's living beings; extremely invisible,

children.text: गुरु श्रुति कते सोई ३० अहंशब्द करि जानौ जाहि । एक
children.translated_text: the guru and scripture speak of that. ||30|| Know that which is known by the word 'I';

children.text: सर्बते परे सु आहि ।। देहस्थूल अनेक सु जोय । सो वह
children.translated_text: it is the one supreme [reality] beyond all. The body is gross and manifold;

children.text: पुरुष सु कैसे होय ३१ हों द्रष्टा विषयादिक को पुनि । देह दृश्य
children.translated_text: how can that be the person? ||31|| I am the seer of sense-objects and the rest; the body

children.text: यह ताहि जानि सुनि ।। मम यह देह ब्योहार सु जोय । पुरुष
children.translated_text: is the seen — know this and listen. 'This body is mine' — this being the convention,

children.text: देह कैसे करि होय ३२ हों बिकार षट रहित सु जोई । देह सदा
children.translated_text: how can the person be the body? ||32|| I am free from the six modifications;

children.text: बिकार युत सोई ।। यह साक्षातप्रत्यक्ष प्रमान । कैसे होय सु
children.translated_text: the body is always endowed with modifications. This is the direct, perceptual proof;

children.text: देह पुमान ३३ सबते परे पुरुष है जोई । श्रुति तेहि लक्षण
children.translated_text: how can the body be the person? ||33|| The person who is beyond all —

children.text: कहत सुजोई ।। ज्ञानिन करके बर्णित जोय । पुरुष देह कैसे
children.translated_text: scripture describes his characteristics. As described by the wise,
how can the person be the body? ||34||
[Hindi commentary:] O fool, listen — the Self that exists, scripture and reasoning
'Everything is <s>Puruṣa</s> (the Person) alone' — in the <s>sūkta</s> (hymn) named '<s>Puruṣa</s>'
this is also declared by <s>śruti</s>; how can that person be identical with the body? ||35||
The person is declared to be unattached in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> [<s>Upaniṣad</s>] as well;
being connected with infinite impurity [as body], how can that person be identical with the body? ||36||
And therein [in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>] it is proclaimed: 'the person is indeed self-luminous';
being inert and illuminated by another, how can that [body] be identical with the person? ||37||
Even by the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s> (ritual portion [of the <s>Veda</s>]), the Self is declared to be distinct from the body;
and being eternal, it enjoys the fruits [of actions] even after the fall of the body. ||38||
And the subtle body (<s>liṅga</s>) is conjoined with many [constituents], moving, visible, and subject to modification;
non-pervasive and of unreal form — how then can this be the person? ||39||

children.text: सबये परम पुरुषहै जोई । ब्रह्मसूक्त मै कह्योंजसोई ।। निश्च-
य श्रुति जेहि कहत प्रमान । कैसे होय सुदेह पुमान ३५ पुरुष
children.translated_text: Certainly, this is the scriptural proof; how can the body be the person? ||35|| The person

children.text: असंख्य कह्यो श्रुति जोई । वृहदारण्य माहिं कह्यो सोई ।। मल
children.translated_text: is declared unattached by scripture — this is stated in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>.

children.text: अनंत करि लपट्यो जोय । देह आत्माकैसे होय ३६ ताही वृह-
children.translated_text: Being entangled in infinite impurity, how can the body be the Self? ||36|| In that very <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>,

children.text: दारण्य के मांहि । स्वयं ज्योति कह्यो पुरुष जु ताहि ।। तन जड़
children.translated_text: the person is called self-luminous. The body being inert

children.text: पर प्रकाश्य सु जोई । देह आत्मा कैसे होई ३७ कर्म काण्ड में
children.translated_text: and illuminated by another, how can the body be the Self? ||37|| In the <s>karmakāṇḍa</s>

children.text: कह्यो जु सोई । देहते भिन्न आत्मा जोई ।। नित्य कर्म फल भु-
children.translated_text: it is said that the Self is different from the body. Being eternal, it enjoys the fruits of action

children.text: क्तै जातें । देह पात के भये सुतातें ३८ लिंग अनेक युक्तहे जोई ।
children.translated_text: after the fall of the body. ||38|| The subtle body is conjoined with many [elements];

children.text: चंचल दृश्य विकारिक सोई ।। असत रूप अब्यापक जोय । सो
children.translated_text: it is restless, visible, and subject to modification. Of unreal form and non-pervasive —
how can that be the Self? ||39||
[Hindi:] Everything is the supreme person — this is what the <s>Brahmasūkta</s> says.
Thus, the Self is other than both [gross and subtle] bodies — the person, the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>);
the Self of all, of the form of all, and beyond all — I am the imperishable. ||40||
Thus, by [analyzing] the Self-portion and the body-portion, the reality of the phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>)
as stated by logic and scripture — what then of the pursuit of the human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>)? ||41||
Thus, by the distinction of Self and body, the identity of the Self with the body has been negated;
now, the unreality of the distinction of bodies is clearly stated. ||42||
Because consciousness is of one form, distinction is never justified;
the state of being a <s>jīva</s> (individual soul) should be known as false, just as [the perception of] a snake in a rope. ||43||
Just as, from ignorance of the rope, in an instant the rope
appears as a snake — so too, consciousness alone, in the form of the universe, is absolute (<s>kevala</s>). ||44||

children.text: ऐसे दोऊ देहते न्यारो । आत्मा पुरुष जव ईश्वर प्यारो ।। स-
र्वात्मा सबरूप जु सोई । सर्ब परे हो अव्यय सोई ४० आतम
children.translated_text: The Self of all, of the form of all — beyond all, imperishable. ||40|| The Self
is different from the body — understand this; the world is unreal, know it as real [only as <s>Brahman</s>].

children.text: बर्णितजोय । यामें कह पुरुषारथ सोय ४१ आत्मा देह भेद करि
children.translated_text: As described by logic and scripture, what is the human goal (<s>puruṣārtha</s>) therein? ||41|| The Self and body — the distinction

children.text: जोई । तनआत्मत्व निवास्यो सोई ।। अब तन भेद असत्यसु
children.translated_text: having been made, the Self-nature of the body has been negated. Now, the unreality of bodily distinction —

children.text: जैसे । सोअस्पष्ट कहतहौं तैसे ४२ चेतन एकरूपजोआहि । भेद
children.translated_text: I shall state it clearly. ||42|| Consciousness is of one form;

children.text: युक्ति सो कथहूं नाहि ।। जीव भाव मिथ्या करिजानि। ज्यों रजु
children.translated_text: distinction is not justified in any way. Know the state of being a <s>jīva</s> as false,

children.text: माहिं सर्प बुधि ठानि ४३ रजु अज्ञान ते छिन इक जोई । जैसे
children.translated_text: just as the intellect superimposes a snake upon a rope. ||43|| From ignorance of the rope, in one instant,

children.text: सर्पनिरजुहै सोई ।। तैसे चेतन है साक्षात । बिश्व रूपकरि सो
children.translated_text: just as the rope appears as a snake, so consciousness is directly [present],
appearing in the form of the universe. ||44||
[Hindi:] Thus, different from both bodies is the Self, the person, the beloved Lord.
The material cause (<s>upādāna</s>) of the phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>) is none other than <s>Brahman</s>;
therefore, this entire phenomenal world is <s>Brahman</s> alone, and not anything else. ||45||
The pervaded and the pervader are false; from the teaching that 'everything is the Self' —
when this supreme reality (<s>tattva</s>) is known, whence is there occasion for difference? ||46||
Multiplicity has indeed been negated by <s>śruti</s> in its own words;
when the non-dual cause is established, how can there be another appearance? ||47||
The fault too has been prescribed by <s>śruti</s>: 'he goes from death to death'
— the person who sees multiplicity here, deceived by <s>māyā</s> (illusion). ||48||
From <s>Brahman</s>, from the Supreme Self, all beings are born;
therefore, one should ascertain that these are <s>Brahman</s> alone. ||49||

children.text: ब्रह्महि कारण जगको जानो । ताबिन कोई चौर न मानो ।।
ताते यह प्रपंच सबजोई । ब्रह्महि है नहिं और जु कोई ४५
children.translated_text: Therefore this entire phenomenal world is <s>Brahman</s> alone, and nothing else. ||45||

children.text: व्याप्य औ व्यापक मिथ्या जानौ । सर्बमात्म इमि बचन सु-
children.translated_text: Know the pervaded and the pervader as false; accept the teaching 'everything is the Self.'

children.text: मानौ ।। ऐसे जान्यौ परम तत्त्व जब । भेद बुद्धि फिर कहों कहां
children.translated_text: When the supreme reality is thus known, where then is the intellect of difference?

children.text: तब ४६ निज मुख निश्चय करिके जोई । श्रुति ना तत्त्वनिवा-
children.translated_text: ||46|| Having made certain by its own words, scripture

children.text: स्योसोई ।। कैसे द्वैत भासहै तबै । अद्वय ब्रह्म भयोयिर जबै ४७
children.translated_text: has negated that very reality [of multiplicity]. How can duality appear when

children.text: भेद दृष्टि श्रुति बिहित सुजानि । जन्म मरण तेहि होतहै मानि ।।
children.translated_text: the non-dual <s>Brahman</s> has come into being [i.e., is realized]? ||47|| Know the vision of difference as prescribed by scripture [as a fault];

children.text: यह नानत्व बिलोकै जोई । माया करि वंचित नर सोई ।।
children.translated_text: accept that birth and death result from it. He who perceives this multiplicity

children.text: ४८ परमात्मा अरु ब्रह्म सुजोई । सर्ब भूत ताते भये सोई ।।
children.translated_text: is a person deceived by <s>māyā</s>.

children.text: ताते इनको ब्रह्महि जानौ । ब्रह्म बिना कछु और न मानौ ४९ ।।
children.translated_text: ||48|| The Supreme Self and <s>Brahman</s> — from that, all beings have come into existence.
[Hindi:] Know <s>Brahman</s> as the cause of the world; accept no other thief [i.e., imposter].
<s>Brahman</s> alone [bears] all names, and the various forms,
and even all actions — so the <s>śruti</s> has proclaimed. ||50||
Just as what is born from gold has the nature of gold eternally,
so what is born from <s>Brahman</s> would likewise have the nature of <s>Brahman</s>. ||51||
Having made even the slightest difference between the <s>jīvātman</s> (individual self) and the <s>Paramātman</s> (Supreme Self),
the deluded person who remains [in that view] — fear is declared for him. ||52||
Where, from ignorance, duality exists — there another sees [difference];
but when everything is known as the Self — there is no 'other' whatsoever. ||53||
For one who knows all beings as the Self itself,
there is no delusion nor sorrow, since there is no second. ||54||

children.text: नाम रूप सब बिबिध सुजोई । ब्रह्म बिना कछु औरनहोई ।
कर्महु सकल ब्रह्म ही जान । यह श्रुति निश्चय कहत प्रमान
children.translated_text: Know all actions too as <s>Brahman</s> alone; this is what scripture declares with certainty as proof.

children.text: ५० सुबरण ते उपज्यो है जौन । सो निश्चय सुबरण है तौन ।।
children.translated_text: ||50|| Whatever is born from gold, that is certainly gold.

children.text: ब्रह्मसों उपजो ब्रह्महि जानौ । यामें संशय कछू न मानौ ५१
children.translated_text: What is born from <s>Brahman</s>, know it as <s>Brahman</s>; admit no doubt in this. ||51||

children.text: जीवात्मा परमातम माहीं । थोरो भेद करत जो आहीं ।। सो मू-
children.translated_text: Between the <s>jīvātman</s> and the <s>Paramātman</s>, one who makes even a slight difference —

children.text: ढ़ात्मा निश्चय जानौ । जन्म मरण भयताहि पिछानौ ५२ जा
children.translated_text: know him certainly as a deluded soul; recognize that birth and death are his [lot]. ||52|| Where

children.text: अज्ञान ते द्वैत सुहोई । और तहां देखत है सोई ।। आत्मा सर्ब
children.translated_text: from ignorance duality arises, another sees [something] there.

children.text: जबै यह जानौ । नहीं और तहँ निश्चय मानौ ५३ जब सब भूत
children.translated_text: When the Self is known as everything, know with certainty: there is nothing else there. ||53|| When all beings

children.text: आत्मा जान्यो । तासु द्वैत भ्रम सबै बिलान्यो ।। नहिं तेहि शोक
children.translated_text: are known as the Self, then all the delusion of duality vanishes.

children.text: मोह भय जोई । अद्वितीय जानेते सोई ५४ ।।
children.translated_text: There is no sorrow, delusion, or fear for that one — from knowing the non-dual. ||54||
[Hindi:] All names and various forms — there is nothing other than <s>Brahman</s>.
This Self is indeed <s>Brahman</s>, abiding as the Self of all —
thus it is determined, having heard the teaching of the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s>. ||55||
Though this world is experienced, and though it is capable of conventional activity,
it is unreal, like a dream, sublated in the subsequent moment. ||56||
Dream [does not exist] in waking; the waking world [does not exist] in dream;
neither of the two exists in deep sleep, and deep sleep [does not exist] in either of the two. ||57||
All three [states] are false, being constructed by the three <s>guṇas</s>;
the witness of these, beyond the <s>guṇas</s>, is the eternal, sole, conscious Self. ||58||
Just as [there is] the illusion of a pot in clay, and the appearance of silver in a shell,
so the state of being a <s>jīva</s> in <s>Brahman</s> is seen when examined. ||59||

children.text: यह जीवात्मा ब्रह्महिजाने । सर्बात्मक ताकोयहि माने ।। यह
निर्द्धार कियो श्रुति सही । वृहदारण्य विषयलोकही ५५ या जग
children.translated_text: This is the determination made by scripture — in the <s>Bṛhadāraṇyaka</s> topic indeed. ||55|| The activities of this world

children.text: के व्योहार तु जोई । अनुभव करिके देरव्यो सोई ।। असत रूप
children.translated_text: are experienced [and then] shown. Of unreal form,

children.text: ज्यों सुप्ना जोय । जागतही नाश्यो सब सोय ५६ स्वप्नो जाग्रत
children.translated_text: like a dream — upon waking, all that is destroyed. ||56|| Dream does not exist

children.text: में नहिं होई । जाग्रत स्वप्न माहिं नहिं कोई ।। दो सुषुप्त माहिं
children.translated_text: in waking; waking does not exist in dream. Both do not exist in deep sleep;

children.text: नहिं पइये ।। दोउनमें सुषुप्त नहिं लहिये ५७ तातें तीनों मिथ्या
children.translated_text: deep sleep is not found in either of the two. ||57|| Therefore, know all three as false;

children.text: जानौ । तीनों गुण करि निर्मित मानौ ।। इनको द्रष्टा एक सु
children.translated_text: accept that they are constructed by the three <s>guṇas</s>. The seer of these is the one

children.text: जोई । गुणातीत चित नित्य जु सोई ५८ ज्यों मृतिका घट भ्रांति
children.translated_text: who is beyond the <s>guṇas</s>, conscious, and eternal. ||58|| Just as there is the illusion of a pot in clay,

children.text: सु जोई ।। शुक्तिमें रजत भ्रमहै सोई ।। त्यों ब्रह्म माहिं जीव भ्रम
children.translated_text: and the delusion of silver in a shell,

children.text: होई । किये बिचार न दीखै कोई ५९ ।।
children.translated_text: so there is the delusion of <s>jīva</s> in <s>Brahman</s>; upon investigation, none [of these] is seen. ||59||
[Hindi:] Know this <s>jīvātman</s> as <s>Brahman</s>; accept it as the Self of all.
Just as in clay [there is the name] 'pot,' in gold [the name] 'bracelet,'
in a shell [the name] 'silver' — so too the word '<s>jīva</s>' in the Supreme. ||60||
Just as blueness in the sky, just as water in a desert,
just as personhood in a post — so too is the universe in the conscious Self. ||61||
Just as a ghost in emptiness, just as the city of the <s>Gandharvas</s>,
just as a double moon in the sky — so is the existence of the world in the Real. ||62||
Just as water itself shines abundantly through waves and ripples,
and just as copper [shines] in the form of a vessel — so too is the nature of the Self (<s>Ātman</s>) in the multitude of cosmic eggs (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>). || 63 ||
Just as earth [is known] by the name 'pot,' and threads by the name 'cloth,'
so consciousness shines by the name 'world' — it should be known through the absence of those [names]. || 64 ||

children.text: ज्यों मृतिका घटनाम कहावै । बहुरिकनक कुण्डलसुबतावै ।।
शुक्ति रजत कर जानै जैसे । ब्रह्म माहिं कहें जीव सुतैसे ६०

children.translated_text: and threads are called by the name 'cloth' — so too the world by name is <s>Brahman</s> itself;

[Vernacular:] Just as clay is called by the name 'pot,' and much gold is beautifully fashioned into an earring,
All conventional activity (<s>vyavahāra</s>) is carried out by people through <s>Brahman</s> alone;
through ignorance (<s>ajñāna</s>), they do not know — just as clay alone [is the reality of] pots and the like. || 65 ||
The cause-effect relation between the pot and clay is eternal, just as [it always is];
so too here, by <s>śruti</s> (scripture) and reasoning, [the relation between] the phenomenal world (<s>prapañca</s>) and <s>Brahman</s> [is established]. || 66 ||
Just as when a pot is grasped, clay is indeed grasped by force,
so too when the phenomenal world is grasped, <s>Brahman</s> alone shines, luminous. || 67 ||
The <s>Ātman</s> (Self) is always pure, yet it always appears as impure;
just as a rope [appears] in two ways to the knower and the ignorant, day and night. || 68 ||
Just as a pot is made of clay, so too is the body made of consciousness (<s>cinmaya</s>);
this distinction between <s>Ātman</s> and non-<s>Ātman</s> is falsely made by the wise [who speak conventionally]. || 69 ||

The <s>śruti</s> (scripture) speaks of <s>prārabdha</s> only for the instruction of the ignorant. (97)
All his <s>karmas</s> (actions) are destroyed when that Supreme, higher and lower, is seen;
to negate the multiplicity [of karma], the <s>śruti</s> and the <s>Gītā</s> have clearly declared this. (98)
If this [prārabdha] is forcibly asserted by the so-called wise, then two defects follow:
the loss of the <s>Vedānta</s> position, since the <s>śruti</s> declares that [liberation comes] through <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge). (99)

children.text: जैसे रज्जु त्यागि कै जोई । सर्प कहतहैं भ्रमते सोई ।।
तैसे ब्रह्म छोड़िकै जौन । मूढ़बुद्धि जग देखत तौन ९५
children.translated_text: so too, leaving <s>Brahman</s> aside, the deluded mind sees the world as such. (95)

children.text: रज्जुको ज्ञान भयो जब जाको । सर्प दूरिभयो तबहीं ताको ।।
children.translated_text: When knowledge of the rope arises for someone, the serpent is removed for them at once;

children.text: तैसे ब्रह्महि जान्यों जबही । जगत कहूँ पैयत नहिं तबहीं ९६ ताको
children.translated_text: likewise, when <s>Brahman</s> is known, the world is not found anywhere. (96) When that [world]

children.text: असत्य करि जान्यो जबै । प्रारब्ध कहँ पैये तबै ।। अज्ञ न बोध
children.translated_text: is known as unreal, then where can <s>prārabdha</s> be found? For the instruction of the ignorant, the <s>śruti</s>

children.text: हेतु श्रुति जोई । प्रारब्ध बरणन कियो सोई ९७ आतम दृष्टि
children.translated_text: has described <s>prārabdha</s>. (97) When the vision of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self)

children.text: हेतु श्रुति जोई । प्रारब्ध बरणन कियो सोई ९७ आतम दृष्टि
children.translated_text: has described <s>prārabdha</s>. (97) When the vision of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self)

children.text: भये ते जौन । सकल कर्म क्षय होतहै तौन ।। प्रारब्ध तब कैसेरहै ।
children.translated_text: arises, all <s>karmas</s> (actions) are destroyed. Then how can <s>prārabdha</s> remain?

children.text: श्रुति यह बचन प्रकट ही कहै ९८ अज्ञ कहै अज्ञान सु जोई । यह
children.translated_text: The <s>śruti</s> openly declares this statement. (98) What the ignorant call ignorance, saying

children.text: प्रारब्ध अमिटहै सोई ।। तब द्वै दोष प्राप्त भय जबै । ते दोउदोष कहत
children.translated_text: that this <s>prārabdha</s> is indestructible, then two faults are obtained. Now I state

children.text: हौं अबै ।। निर्मोक्ष प्रसंग एक जोई । द्वितिय दोष अव सुनिये
children.translated_text: those two faults: the first is the impossibility of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation);

children.text: सोई ।। ज्ञान संप्रदाय छेद यह जौन । दूजो दोष यहीहै तौन ।। पुनि
children.translated_text: now hear the second fault: the cutting off of the tradition of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),

children.text: वेदांत मत हानि सु होई । यह निश्चय करिजानौ सोई ।। जाते
children.translated_text: that is the second fault. Furthermore, the loss of the <s>Vedānta</s> position follows;

children.text: ज्ञान होत निश्चयकरि । सो श्रुति कहत न हिय संसयधरि ९९ ।।
children.translated_text: know this with certainty. That through which <s>jñāna</s> arises, the <s>śruti</s> declares it without doubt in the heart. (99)
[Hindi commentary:] Just as one who, abandoning the rope, calls it a serpent, wanders in delusion,
Now I shall describe the fifteen limbs for the attainment of the aforementioned [realization];
through all of these, one should always practice <s>nididhyāsana</s> (deep meditation) alone. (100)
Without constant practice, the attainment of <s>Saccidātman</s> (the Self of being and consciousness) does not occur;
therefore, the seeker of the highest good should contemplate <s>Brahman</s> through <s>nididhyāsana</s> for a long time. (101)
<s>Yama</s> (restraint), <s>niyama</s> (observance), <s>tyāga</s> (renunciation), <s>mauna</s> (silence), <s>deśa</s> (place), and <s>kāla</s> (time),
<s>āsana</s> (posture), <s>mūlabandha</s> (root lock), <s>dehasāmya</s> (bodily equilibrium), and <s>dṛksthiti</s> (steadiness of gaze), (102)
<s>prāṇasaṃyamana</s> (breath control), <s>pratyāhāra</s> (sense withdrawal), and <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration),
<s>ātmadhyāna</s> (meditation on the Self), and <s>samādhi</s> (absorption) — these are the limbs declared in order. (103)
The restraint of the group of senses through the understanding that all is <s>Brahman</s>
is called <s>yama</s> (restraint); it should be practiced again and again. (104)

children.text: अब रस पञ्च अंगहैं जोई । ज्ञान प्राप्त हित कहौं सु जोई ।। ते
सब करिये योग लु ज्ञानि । सदा निदि ध्यासन यह मानि १००
children.translated_text: All of these should be practiced, O wise one, knowing this always as <s>nididhyāsana</s> (deep meditation). (100)

children.text: नित अभ्यास बिना नहिं होई । आत्माकी प्रापतिहै जोई ।। ताते
children.translated_text: Without daily practice, the attainment of the <s>Ātman</s> (Self) does not occur. Therefore,

children.text: ब्रह्म निदिध्यासन कर । जिज्ञासूको श्रेय होयवर १०१ यम अरु
children.translated_text: practice <s>Brahma-nididhyāsana</s> (contemplation on <s>Brahman</s>); for the seeker, the highest good shall come. (101) <s>Yama</s> (restraint) and

children.text: नियम त्याग पुनि मौन । देश अरु काल पिछानै तौन ।। आसन
children.translated_text: <s>niyama</s> (observance), <s>tyāga</s> (renunciation), then <s>mauna</s> (silence); <s>deśa</s> (place) and <s>kāla</s> (time), know them well.

children.text: मूल बंध पुनि जोई । तन सम करै दृष्टि थिर होई १०२ प्राणा-
children.translated_text: <s>Āsana</s> (posture) and <s>mūlabandha</s> (root lock); making the body balanced, the gaze becomes steady. (102) <s>Prāṇā-</s>

children.text: याम करै पुनि जौन । प्रत्याहार धारणा तौन ।। आत्मा ध्यान
children.translated_text: <s>yāma</s> (breath control) one should then perform; <s>pratyāhāra</s> (sense withdrawal) and <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration).

children.text: समाधि सु जोई । क्रमते अंग कह्यो सब सोई १०३ ।। अथ यम
children.translated_text: <s>Ātma-dhyāna</s> (meditation on the Self) and <s>samādhi</s> (absorption), all these limbs have been described in order. (103) Now <s>yama</s> (restraint)

children.text: कहियेहैं ।। सब जग ब्रह्महिहै यह जोई । या करि सब इंद्रिन
children.translated_text: is described: All the world is <s>Brahman</s> alone; through this understanding, the restraint of all the senses

children.text: दम होई ।। यम वह कह्यो सु उत्तम जोई । बार बार अभ्यास
children.translated_text: occurs. That <s>yama</s> is called the highest; practice it
again and again. (104)
[Hindi commentary:] Now the fifteen limbs that exist for the attainment of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge), I shall describe them.
The flow of similar [thoughts] (<s>sajātīya-pravāha</s>) and the rejection of dissimilar [thoughts] (<s>vijātīya-tiraskṛti</s>)—
this is <s>niyama</s> (observance), which is supreme bliss; <s>niyama</s> is practiced by the wise. (105)
<s>Tyāga</s> (renunciation) is [the abandonment] of the form of the phenomenal world through the vision of the <s>Cidātman</s> (consciousness-Self);
<s>tyāga</s> is revered by the great, since it immediately becomes the form of liberation. (106)
That from which speech turns back, not reaching it, along with the mind—
that <s>mauna</s> (silence), attainable by <s>yogīs</s>, should always be [practiced] by the wise. (107)
That from which speech turns back—who can speak of it?
If the phenomenal world is to be spoken of, even that is devoid of words. (108)
Thus, or that, becomes <s>mauna</s> (silence), called the natural [state] (<s>sahaja</s>) of the virtuous;
the silence of speech is prescribed for the ignorant by the knowers of <s>Brahman</s>. (109)

children.text: अथ नियम कहिये हैं ।। ब्रह्माकार वृत्ति करैजोई ।। जगता
कार बृति तजि सोई ।। नियम सो याको नाम कहावै । नियम
children.translated_text: abandoning the world-formed thought-wave—that is called <s>niyama</s> by name;

children.text: ते परानन्द बुध पावै १०५ अथ त्याग कहिये हैं ।। एक आत्मा
children.translated_text: through <s>niyama</s>, the wise attain supreme bliss. (105) Now <s>tyāga</s> (renunciation) is described: One who sees the one <s>Ātman</s> (Self) alone,

children.text: देखत जोई । नाम रूप सब त्याग सु होई ।। त्यागमहत करि
children.translated_text: for them the renunciation of all names and forms occurs. <s>Tyāga</s> is revered by the great, and

children.text: पूजित यातें । सद्य मोक्ष मय होत सुजातें १०६ अथ मौन कहिये
children.translated_text: from that, one immediately attains the form of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). (106) Now <s>mauna</s> (silence) is described:

children.text: हैं ।। बाचा करिकै कह्यो न जाहि । मनहूंपाय सकैनहिं ताहि ।।
children.translated_text: That which cannot be spoken of by speech, that which even the mind cannot attain—

children.text: याते मौन सुयोगी जानै । सो बुध सदा रूप निज मानै १०७
children.translated_text: from this, the accomplished <s>yogī</s> knows silence; the wise one always considers it one's own true nature. (107)

children.text: बाचाकहियेहैं ।। बाचाकरि निवृत्ति है जोई । ताको बरणि सकै
children.translated_text: [Hindi commentary:] Speech is described: That from which speech turns back,

children.text: नहिं कोई ।। कहिबे योग प्रपंच है जौन । सोपि शब्द बरजित है
children.translated_text: no one can describe it. The phenomenal world that is fit to be spoken of,

children.text: तौन १०८ यह बिचार ताको कहि मौन ।। सत् पुरुषन में प्रगट
children.translated_text: even that is devoid of words. (108) This reflection is called <s>mauna</s> (silence); among the virtuous it is manifestly

children.text: सुतौने ।। गिरा मौन मूढ़न को जानि । ज्ञानी जनन सुकह्यो
children.translated_text: so. The silence of speech, know it as belonging to the foolish;
the wise have declared and explained this. (109)
[Hindi commentary:] Now <s>niyama</s> (observance) is described: One who cultivates the <s>Brahman</s>-formed thought-wave,
That in which no people exist at the beginning, end, or middle,
by which this [universe] is pervaded at all times — that <s>deśa</s> (place) is solitary and immortal. (110)
By the reckoning of all beings from <s>Brahmā</s> onward, in the twinkling [of an eye],
that which is indicated by the word <s>kāla</s> (time) is indeed the undivided, non-dual bliss. (111)
That in which the contemplation of <s>Brahman</s> occurs easily and ceaselessly—
know that to be the [true] <s>āsana</s> (posture); no other is a comfortable posture. (112)
The <s>siddha</s> (accomplished) [posture] is that which is the beginningless source of all beings, the imperishable substratum of the universe,
in which the <s>siddha</s> (perfected one) rests absorbed — that indeed is <s>siddhāsana</s> (the accomplished posture). (113)
That which is the root of all beings — the root-lock of the mind,
<s>mūlabandha</s> (the root lock) should always be practiced; it is fit for the <s>rājayogīs</s> (royal yogis). (114)

children.text: अथ देश कहिये हैं ।। आदि अन्त पुनि मध्य के माहीं । आत्मा
में जगदीसत नाहीं ।। यामें सदा व्याप्त है जोई । बिजनदेश
children.translated_text: the world is not seen in the <s>Ātman</s> (Self). That by which [everything] is always pervaded, that solitary <s>deśa</s> (place)

children.text: कहियतहै सोई ११० ।। अथकाल कहिये हैं ।। ब्रह्मादिक सब भूत है
children.translated_text: is what is spoken of. (110) Now <s>kāla</s> (time) is described: All beings including <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: जोई ।। जानिमेषते थिति लय होई ।। काल शब्द यह जानो ताहि ।
children.translated_text: in the twinkling [of an eye], come into being and are dissolved. Know that as the word <s>kāla</s> (time);

children.text: अखण्डानद सु अद्धय आहि १११ अय सुख आसन कहिये हैं ।।
children.translated_text: it is undivided bliss and non-dual. (111) Now the comfortable <s>āsana</s> (posture) is described:

children.text: सुख थिर रूप ब्रह्म चिंतन महि । कर्तव्यता तहँ चिन्ता है नहि ।।
children.translated_text: In the steady form of blissful <s>Brahman</s> contemplation, there is no anxiety of duty.

children.text: आसन यहहै जानौ ताही । याते और सुखासन नाही ११२ यही-
children.translated_text: Know this to be the [true] <s>āsana</s> (posture); there is no other comfortable posture than this. (112) This same

children.text: सिद्धा सन कहिये हैं ।। जाते सर्ब भूत सिध होई । जग अधिष्ठान
children.translated_text: <s>siddhāsana</s> (accomplished posture) is described: That from which all beings are accomplished, that which is the imperishable substratum of the world—

children.text: जु अव्यय सोई ।। तामें सिद्ध जुलै ह्वै जौन । सिद्धासन कहियत
children.translated_text: one who becomes absorbed and established in that, that is called

children.text: है तौन ११३ अथ मूलबंधन कहिये हैं ।। सब भूतन को मूल सु-
children.translated_text: <s>siddhāsana</s> (the accomplished posture). (113) Now <s>mūlabandha</s> (root lock) is described: That which is the root of all beings,

children.text: जोई । चितको बंधन मूलहै सोई ।। मूल बंध यह सदा जु सोई
children.translated_text: that root is the bondage of the mind. This <s>mūlabandha</s> (root lock), always
to be practiced, belongs to the <s>rājayogīs</s> (royal yogis). (114)
[Hindi commentary:] Now <s>deśa</s> (place) is described: In the beginning, end, and middle,
Know the equilibrium of the limbs to be absorption in the supreme <s>Brahman</s>;
otherwise, there is no equality — [mere] straightness is like a dry tree. (115)
Making the gaze filled with knowledge, one sees the world as pervaded by <s>Brahman</s>;
that gaze is supremely noble, not the one that looks at the tip of the nose. (116)
Where there is cessation of the seer, seeing, and the seen,
the gaze should be fixed there alone, not at the tip of the nose. (117)
Through the contemplation of <s>Brahman</s>-nature in all mental states such as <s>citta</s> (mind) and so forth,
the cessation of all <s>vṛttis</s> (mental modifications) — that is called <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control). (118)
The negation of the phenomenal world is called <s>recaka</s> (exhalation);
the thought-wave 'I am <s>Brahman</s> alone' is declared to be <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation). (119)

children.text: अथ देह साम्य कहियेहैं ।। सब अगन सम जानहु यातें । सम
आत्मा में लैकै तातें ।। समानत्वयह जानौसोर्ह ।शुष्क वृक्ष बल
children.translated_text: they are absorbed in the one <s>Ātman</s> (Self). This equality should be known;

children.text: सम नहिं होई ११५ अथ दृष्टि ठहरावना कहियेहैं ।। दृष्टि ज्ञान
children.translated_text: [mere] straightness like a dry tree is not [true] equality. (115) Now the steadying of the gaze is described: One who makes the gaze

children.text: मय करै सु जौन । देखै ब्रह्म रूप जग तौन ।। दृष्टि पाय उदारहै
children.translated_text: filled with <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge) sees the world as the form of <s>Brahman</s>. Having attained that gaze, it is truly noble;

children.text: सोई । नहिं नासाग्र बिलोकन जोई ११६ दृष्टा दृष्ट दृश्यहै जौन ।
children.translated_text: it is not the gazing at the tip of the nose. (116) The seer, the seen, and the sight—

children.text: सब त्रिपुटीब्र लखी है तौन ।। दृष्टि वही करतब्यहै सोई । नहिं
children.translated_text: when the triad is perceived as <s>Brahman</s>, that very gaze should be maintained;

children.text: नासाग्र बिलोकि न जोई ११७ अथ प्राणायाम कहिये हैं ।। चित्ता
children.translated_text: it is not the gazing at the tip of the nose. (117) Now <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) is described: In all states of mind (<s>citta</s>)

children.text: दिक सब भावन माहीं । ब्रह्म रूप करि जानै ताहीं ।। सब बृत्तिन
children.translated_text: and so on, one should know them as the form of <s>Brahman</s>. Through the cessation of all <s>vṛttis</s> (mental modifications),

children.text: निरोध द्वै यातें ।। प्राणायाम सु कहियत तातें ११८ यह प्रपंच सब
children.translated_text: it is called <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control). (118) This entire phenomenal world is

children.text: मिथ्या जौन । रेचकनाम कहावैतौन ।। मैं हौं ब्रह्मवृत्तियह जोई।
children.translated_text: false — that is called <s>recaka</s> (exhalation). The thought-wave 'I am <s>Brahman</s>'—
that is called <s>pūraka</s> (inhalation). (119)
[Hindi commentary:] Now <s>dehasāmya</s> (bodily equilibrium) is described: Know all the limbs as equal, because
Thereafter, the steadiness of the true thought-wave is <s>kumbhaka</s> (breath retention), the restraint of <s>prāṇa</s> (vital breath);
this [is the practice] of the awakened ones; for the ignorant, it is [merely] the torment of breath. (120)
Having seen the Self-nature in sense objects, the dissolution of the mind in <s>citta</s> (consciousness)—
this should be known as <s>pratyāhāra</s> (sense withdrawal); it should be practiced by seekers of liberation. (121)
Wherever the mind goes, seeing <s>Brahman</s> there,
the holding of the mind [in <s>Brahman</s>] — that <s>dhāraṇā</s> (concentration) is the supreme delight. (122)
Through the true thought-wave 'I am <s>Brahman</s> alone,' abiding without any support—
known by the name <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), bestowing supreme bliss. ||123||
Through the modification (<s>vṛtti</s>) that is free from change (<s>nirvikāra</s>), and again through [that modification] that has the form of <s>Brahman</s>,
the complete forgetting of [all other] modifications — this is called knowledge-<s>samādhi</s> (absorption in knowledge). ||124||

children.text: सो सद्वृति सुनिश्चल होई । कुम्भक नाम कहावै सोई ।।
प्राणायाम सु ज्ञानिन को यह । घ्राण दबावन अज्ञन कोकह १२०
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] This is the <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath control) of the knowledgeable; pressing the nostrils is [the prāṇāyāma] of the ignorant. ||120||

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] goes, one should see <s>Brahman</s> there. From that, the mind becomes concentrated.

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] That is called <s>dhāraṇā</s>. ||122|| Now meditation on the <s>Ātman</s> is described: 'I am

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] <s>Brahman</s>' — that true modification (<s>vṛtti</s>) which is unsupported and steady —

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] know that as <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation); recognize it as the bestower of supreme bliss. ||123|| Now <s>samādhi</s>

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] is described: That changeless dual modification which becomes of the form of <s>Brahman</s> —

children.text: और वृत्ति सब भुल सुजाहि । ज्ञान समाधि सु कहियेताहि ९२४ ।।
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] and all other modifications are forgotten — that is called <s>jñāna-samādhi</s> (knowledge-absorption). ||124||
[Hindi:] That good modification (<s>vṛtti</s>) which becomes steady — that is called <s>kumbhaka</s> (breath retention).
Having known this unartificial bliss, the good [seeker] should practice [it] well,
until it comes under one's control, so that when applied it may arise again in an instant. ||125||
Then, freed from [all] means, one becomes accomplished — a king of <s>yogins</s>;
and the nature of that [state] is not an object of the mind or of speech. ||126||
When <s>samādhi</s> is being practiced, obstacles come forcibly:
absence of inquiry (<s>anusandhāna</s>), laziness, craving for enjoyment, ||127||
<s>laya</s> (dissolution/sleep), <s>tamas</s> (dullness), distraction (<s>vikṣepa</s>), tasting of [blissful] flavor, and voidness (<s>śūnyatā</s>).
Such multitudes of obstacles should be gradually abandoned by knowers of <s>Brahman</s>. ||128||
Through a modification of being (<s>bhāva-vṛtti</s>), [one attains] the state of being; through a modification of void (<s>śūnya-vṛtti</s>), voidness;
through a <s>Brahman</s>-modification, fullness — therefore one should practice that fullness. ||129||

children.text: यह आनन्द अकृत्रिम जोई । जानि साधु अभ्यास करै सोई ।।
जबलग पुरुषके बश यह जोय । छिन महँ मनके लगावतहोय १२५

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] [means] sleep; <s>tamas</s> [means] non-discrimination between what should and should not be done; distraction [means] remembrance of sense-objects; tasting of flavor

[Hindi:] [means] a modification of the form 'how blessed am I!' and such bliss; voidness [means] a defect of the mind — [these are] the latent impressions (<s>vāsanās</s>) of attachment, aversion, etc.

children.text: सनयी ।। भाववृत्तितेभाव सु जोई । शून्यवृत्तितेशून्य जुसोई ।।
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] Through a modification of being, there is being; through a modification of void, there is voidness.

children.text: ब्रह्मवृत्ति तें पूरन ब्रह्म जौन । सोइपूर्णत्व अभ्यासेतौन १२९ ।।
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] Through a <s>Brahman</s>-modification, there is full <s>Brahman</s> — therefore one should practice that fullness. ||129||
[Hindi:] This bliss which is unartificial — knowing it, the good person should practice it.
Those who, having abandoned this supreme modification called <s>Brahman</s>,
live in vain — they are equal to animals. ||130||
Those who know this modification, and having known it, increase it —
they are truly the blessed among good persons; they are worthy of worship in the three worlds. ||131||
Those in whom this modification has grown and has fully matured —
they truly have attained <s>Brahman</s>-hood; not so [for] mere proclaimers of <s>Brahman</s>. ||132||
Those who are skilled in talk about <s>Brahman</s> but devoid of the [<s>Brahman</s>-]modification, [and are] greatly attached [to sense-objects] —
they, no less [immersed in] the darkness of ignorance, come and go again and again. ||133||
Those who do not remain without the <s>Brahman</s>-filled modification even for half the blink of an eye —
they abide like <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, like <s>Sanaka</s> and the others, like <s>Śuka</s> and the others. ||134||

children.text: परम पावनी ब्रह्मवृत्ति सो । याको त्याग करतहै जन जो ।।

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] live in vain in the world; such persons are equal to animals. ||130||

children.text: ब्रह्मवृत्ति जे जानत अहैं । जानिकै ताहि बढावत रहैं ।। ते
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] Those who know the <s>Brahman</s>-modification, and having known it, continue to increase it —

children.text: सतपुरुष धन्य हैं जोई । बन्दनीय त्रिभुवन में सोई १३१ ।।
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] those true persons are blessed; they are worthy of worship in the three worlds. ||131||

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] Those whose modification has been growing and has become fully matured —

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] they truly attain <s>Brahman</s>; there is no other proclaimer of <s>Brahman</s> [worthy of the name]. ||132||

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] Clever in <s>Brahman</s>-talk, [but] sensual [and] without the <s>Brahman</s>-modification —

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] know them as equal to <s>Brahmā</s> and the others; regard them as equal to <s>Sanaka</s> and the others, <s>Śuka</s> and the others. ||134||
[Hindi:] That supremely purifying <s>Brahman</s>-modification — those who abandon it
The effect-ness [of the effect] has gone into the cause; [but] through the cause, there is no effect-ness;
therefore cause-hood too perishes when the effect is absent, upon inquiry. ||135||
Then the pure reality remains, which is indeed beyond the reach of words —
this should be seen again and again through the example of clay and pot. ||136||
By this very method, the modification becomes of the nature of <s>Brahman</s>;
for those of pure mind, the modification-knowledge arises, and then [comes] what is beyond that. ||137||
Through negative concomitance (<s>vyatireka</s>), one should first perceive the cause [as distinct from the effect];
then through positive concomitance (<s>anvaya</s>), one should see the cause as ever-present in the effect. ||138||
One should see the cause in the effect, then abandon the effect;
cause-hood itself departs on its own — what remains [alone], O sage, is [the reality]. ||139||

Whatever object is contemplated with intense force and with a nature of certainty —
a person quickly becomes that; this should be known [from the example of] the wasp and the caterpillar. ||140||
All this that has the nature of the seer and the seen is of the nature of consciousness (<s>cit</s>);
with constant attentiveness, one should meditate on one's own <s>Ātman</s>. ||141||
Having led the visible to invisibility, one should contemplate in the form of <s>Brahman</s>;
the wise one should abide in eternal bliss, with an intellect filled with the essence of consciousness. ||142||
Endowed with these limbs, [the practice] is called <s>Rāja Yoga</s>;
for those whose impurities are somewhat burned, it is combined with <s>Haṭha Yoga</s>. ||143||
For those whose minds are fully matured, this alone bestows the five <s>siddhis</s> (attainments);
for all who are devoted to the <s>Guru</s> and to God, it is easily attainable and swift. ||144||
Thus ends the Hindi commentary (<s>bhāṣā</s>) on the <s>Aparokṣānubhava</s> text, composed by <s>Jñānadāsa</s>.

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] The wise one abides always in bliss; the intellect attains fullness of the essence of consciousness. ||142|| These limbs, combined with method —

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] the eightfold <s>Yoga</s> together with knowledge [is appropriate]. ||143|| For one whose mind has become mature,

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] for all of them, <s>siddhi</s> comes easily and swiftly. ||144||
[Hindi:] By contemplating intensely, when certainty arises in whatever object —

ज्ञान के फल करि अंत में जौन । लहै कैवल्य शोकगति तौन १
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] at the end, as the fruit of knowledge, attains <s>kaivalya</s> (liberation), [going] beyond grief. ||1||

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] Whether on the road, in excrement and urine, in the house of a <s>caṇḍāla</s>, or in a cremation ground —

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] whether effort was made or none at all — at the end of the body, one attains <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation). ||2||

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] <s>Dohā</s> (couplet): [In the year with] eight <s>Vasus</s>, eight, and the moon [i.e., Saṃvat year 1881], this present year;

children.translated_text: [Hindi:] the fourteenth of the dark half of <s>Kārttika</s>, a Friday — know that. ||1|| In the place of <s>Indraprastha</s>, in the <s>Līlā</s>

children.text: को कटराजान । राम दुवारे में कह्यो ज्ञान दास परमान २ ।।
children.translated_text: [Hindi:] [quarter] of <s>Kaṭrā Jān</s>, at the door of <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Jñānadāsa</s> composed this supreme [text]. ||2||
[Hindi:] Whether in a sacred place or in the house of a low-caste person — one who, having lost [body-]consciousness, abandons the body —
